entries.name: Alternating Expectation Conditional Maximization
entries.definition: A likelihood-optimization framework that alternates cycles of expectation and constrained maximization, permitting the admissible data augmentation and constraint functions to change between cycles while collectively covering the parameter directions.
entries.identity_notes: AECM generalizes fixed-augmentation ECM and partitioned SAGE through cycle-specific augmentations and general constraints. One cycle contains an E-step and one or more CM steps sharing that expectation; an iteration completes the stated space-filling coverage. Working parameters index augmentation choices without changing the observed model. This is distinct from PX-EM expansion/reduction and from Gibbs sampling, even when particular examples have matching updates. aio_mappings.rationale: This deterministic likelihood-fitting algorithm learns model parameters from data. definition_evidence.locator: Section 3.2, Definition 1 and Equations 3.5-3.8, pp.525-527 / PDF 16-18

claims.statement: At the current parameter choose an augmentation that yields the same observed-data model and compute its expected augmented log likelihood conditional on the observed data. Perform the ordered CM steps on that fixed expectation, each on a constraint surface containing the most recent intermediate parameter. Before changing augmentation or starting the next cycle, refresh the expectation at the current parameter. Constraints may be more general than disjoint coordinate blocks.

evidence.locator: Section 3.2, pp.525-527 / PDF 16-18, especially Eq 3.5

claims.statement: The fixed expected objective increases within a cycle, so observed likelihood is nondecreasing between completed cycles and consequently completed iterations. This need not hold between every pair of CM substeps within one frozen-expectation cycle. Parameter-space coverage is additional to ascent: the source groups consecutive cycles into iterations when their constraint-gradient spaces have trivial intersection. The stationary-limit result further requires its stated regularity, interior, CM uniqueness or tie-handling, and iteration-mapping conditions.

evidence.locator: Section 3.2 Eq 3.7-3.8; Section 3.3 Theorems 2-3 and ECME-ordering remark, pp.526-528 / PDF 17-19

claims.statement: For a multivariate t model, the source indexes augmentations by q(a)=|Sigma|^(-a)q. With fixed degrees of freedom nu and dimension p, a=1/(nu+p) gives the weighted location and scatter normalized by the sum of latent weights rather than sample count. For unknown nu, location/scatter and nu updates form different cycles, with the design parameter recomputed from the current fixed nu. This family-specific information comparison does not assert optimality over all augmentations or algorithms.

The general matrix-rate formula assumes convergence to an interior point and a fixed cycle composition with the specified differentiability conditions. It does not imply AECM is always faster than EM. Improving a local asymptotic rate or an individual block step does not guarantee fewer elapsed seconds, and the theorem does not establish convergence at nonnegative parameter boundaries.

evidence.locator: Section 3.3 Theorem 4, p.529 / PDF 20; Section 3.5, p.537 / PDF 28; author reply, p.562 / PDF 53

limitations: Monotone bounded likelihood values alone do not establish parameter convergence or global optimality. Incomplete coverage, inexact unconstrained numerical steps or stale expectations after changing augmentation require separate analysis.

The main paper’s interior convergence results do not automatically cover its Poisson image example at zero intensities; the discussion explicitly refers to separate SAGE analysis. The Poisson pseudobackground example overlaps SAGE3 and is not assigned a duplicate concept ID.
Working-parameter selection may simplify or complicate the E/CM subproblems. A deterministic optimization result is not a posterior-sampling mixing guarantee.

All 58 source PDF pages were inspected, including discussions and author corrections. Historical simulations, CPU comparisons, image reconstructions and author software were not reproduced; no universal speed or clinical-performance claim is made.

definition_evidence.locator: SectionsII-III, Definitions 1-2 and Theorem 1, PDF 2-4
SectionII, Eq 2-5 and hidden-data construction, pp.1418-1419 / PDF 2-3

claims.statement: For active block S, keep the complementary parameters fixed at their current values. An admissible hidden space factors p(y,x;theta)=p(y|x;theta_complement)p(x;theta), with the observation channel independent of theta_S. Increase the conditional expected log p(x;theta) minus the penalty over that block, then carry the updated parameter forward and recompute for the next block. Different blocks need not combine into one common complete-data space. The 1995 extension uses the same block-ascent logic through a surrogate whose improvement lower-bounds actual objective improvement.

evidence.locator: Definitions 1-2, SectionsII-III and Theorem 1, PDF 2-4
SectionII Eq 2-5, pp.1418-1419 / PDF 2-3

claims.statement: For Poisson means m_n=sum_j a_nj lambda_j+r_n with nonnegative coefficients, hold other coordinates at their current values. A valid shift z_k gives hidden means a_nk(lambda_k+z_k) and residual means r_n+sum_(j!=k)a_nj lambda_j-a_nk z_k. With e_k=sum_n a_nk y_n/m_n and positive a_dotk=sum_n a_nk, the unpenalized update is max((lambda_k+z_k)e_k/a_dotk-z_k,0). SAGE2 uses min_(a_nk>0)r_n/a_nk; SAGE3 can use min_(a_nk>0)(r_n+other current contributions)/a_nk. Freeze this shift within the block, update projected means immediately, and refresh the next block. A positive shift can revive an initially zero coordinate.

evidence.locator: SectionsIII-IV and TableI, pp.1419-1423 / PDF 3-7

claims.statement: Valid block surrogates establish objective ascent, while parameter convergence needs additional conditions on curvature, continuity, bounded level sets and repeated coordinate coverage. The 1995 proof must be read with the author corrections: the mixed derivative is continuous in both arguments, and the final Lemma 6 argument is restricted to surrogates separable in their first argument. Its general statement is therefore not used as an unrestricted convergence guarantee for coupled multivariate block surrogates.

evidence.locator: Entry fessler:95:pml, complete errata including final Lemma 6 restriction

claims.statement: The 1994 statement suggesting restoration of old other-pixel estimates is superseded by the 1995 current-coordinate algorithm. The 1994 Theorem 2 proof incorrectly assumes real Gauss-Seidel eigenvalues; the author restricts that proof to the case in which a maximum-magnitude eigenvalue is real. This correction is a limitation of the proof, not by itself a counterexample to every speed comparison.

evidence.locator: Entry fessler:94:sag, scheduling and eigenvalue errata

limitations: Strict concavity alone does not ensure uniformly positive Hessian curvature. The cited convergence conditions, boundary behavior and surrogate separability must be checked for the specific problem.

The source’s Gaussian residual update in the 1994 author copy PDF 8 prints a plus sign after initializing residual=y-A theta. Maintaining that residual instead requires subtracting A times the parameter increment. This curator-identified sign inconsistency is checked in the saved finite example and is separate from the published author errata.

Positive shift values require valid nonnegative hidden and residual means; zero measurement sensitivities are excluded from the minima and a zero column sum cannot use the displayed update. Penalized updates must optimize the penalty-aware surrogate, not blindly reuse the unpenalized formula.

The 1995 errata also correct squared triangle-inequality terms, the factor in J, the sign in Eq 38 and the limiting subscript in Lemma 6. Neither objective ascent nor symmetry of a Hessian establishes a universal rate or global optimum.

Both full papers and relevant author errata were inspected. Finite examples check scheduling, projection bookkeeping, boundary revival, a penalized scalar root and the Gaussian sign/eigenvalue issues; no author implementation, phantom study or clinical reconstruction was reproduced.

claims.statement: At a regular interior fit theta*, let Ic be the conditional expected negative complete-data Hessian and D the EM map derivative using input-coordinate rows and output-coordinate columns. claims.statement: Obtain a tightly converged fit and expected complete information. Perturb one input coordinate away from theta*, holding the other input coordinates at theta*, and perform one full ordinary EM update. Divide each output change from theta* by the input perturbation to approximate one row of D, using stabilized ratios as perturbations approach the fit. Section 3 implements SEM by making CMSTEPS a joint Q maximization and setting the separate CM derivative to zero.

aecm.identity: Alternating expectation-conditional maximization (AECM), Meng and van Dyk 1997; general deterministic likelihood optimization framework combining cycle-specific augmentation and model reduction. Not a model, trained instance, stochastic sampler, or universal acceleration theorem. Working-parameter selection is an approach within this framework, not identical to parameter expansion. The t example can yield the same iterates as PX-EM without making the general algorithms synonyms.
mechanism: Section 3.2, printed 525-527/PDF16-18: a cycle is an E-step followed by one or more ordered constrained maximizations sharing its expected augmented log likelihood. Each next cycle starts a fresh E-step at the current parameter, potentially with a different admissible augmentation and constraint functions. Constraints need not be a fixed disjoint coordinate partition. The complete-data representation must integrate/map back to the same observed model.

Eq3.5 maximizes cycle Q over a constraint surface passing through the most recent CM iterate. Eq3.7-3.8 define an iteration by consecutive cycles whose constraint-gradient spaces have trivial intersection (space filling). Full-rank differentiable constraints, interior parameter setting and repeated completed coverage are explicit assumptions. An arbitrary sequence that never updates part of the parameter does not establish stationarity.

Section3.3 Theorem2 printed527-528/PDF18-19: Q rises throughout a cycle and compared with its E-step anchor; observed likelihood therefore rises at the END of each cycle and iteration, without needing space filling for this monotonicity alone. This does not claim that every individual CM inside one frozen-Q cycle increases observed likelihood.

Printed528/PDF19 remark: Q(theta1|anchor)>=Q(theta2|anchor) implies observed-likelihood improvement in general only when theta2=anchor. Authors identify an invalid assumption in the ECME 1994 proof and require a refreshed E-step whenever augmentation changes; ordering observed-likelihood CM steps after augmented ones accomplishes this because a no-augmentation E-step is the identity. This independently corroborates the previous batch's finite counterexample.

Table2 printed527/PDF18: CM, EM, ECM, multicycle ECM, modified ECME, and partitioned SAGE are contained constructions. SAGE has one CM per cycle and parameter-partition constraints. General AECM permits multiple CMs per cycle and more general constraints. Treat broader-framework containment separately from exact concept equivalence.

Section2.2-2.4 printed515-522/PDF6-13: fixed-nu t model uses scaled latent q(a)=|Sigma|^-a q. Working a indexes augmentation without changing observed t distribution. Under this family a=1/(nu+p) minimizes expected augmented information and changes scatter normalization n to sum_i w_i, with w=(nu+p)/(nu+Mahalanobis distance), while location remains weighted mean. Section3.4 printed529-531/PDF20-22 alternates location/scatter at fixed current nu with a nu update; a is then cycle-dependent. AECM1 uses scaled augmentation for location/scatter, standard scale latent variable for nu; AECM2 uses observed likelihood for nu. Root equations are not a blanket guarantee of a unique global optimum.

Section3.5 printed532-537/PDF23-28: Poisson means sum a_nk lambda_k+r_n, nonnegative known a/r and lambda. Per active pixel partition counts into Z with mean a_nk(lambda_k+beta_k) and residual B with mean r_n+sum_other a_nj lambda_j-a_nk beta_k. Beta is bounded by nonnegative residual means. Optimal per-block beta=min_{a_nk>0}(r_n+other current means)/a_nk, matching SAGE3 pseudobackground from Fessler/Hero1995. E and CM use current other coordinates and projections, updating projected means immediately. The pseudo-code on printed537 correctly increments means by a_nk times the coordinate change. This algorithm is already inside SAGE, so do not invent a separate native record for the Poisson example. Beta in this section is augmentation design, not the smoothing-penalty beta in SAGE1995.

Section4 printed537-538/PDF28-29 draws a deterministic/stochastic analogy. Optimization finds modes; Gibbs/DA targets distributions. This is not an identity or a license to assert arbitrary block sampling has the desired invariant distribution.
limitations: Theorem3 printed528/PDF19 gives stationary LIMIT POINTS under cited Wu1983 regularity, unique CMs (or stated tie handling), fixed iteration mapping and space filling; not unconditional convergence to a unique/global optimizer. Wu's original paper was not newly read here, so do not enumerate unverified imported conditions as though checked.

Theorem4 printed529/PDF20 uses interior convergence, fixed cycle composition, differentiability and Lagrange conditions. It is a matrix-rate expression, NOT a general theorem that AECM is faster than EM. Author reply printed562/PDF53 explicitly corrects Celeux's contrary interpretation and reaffirms that Theorems3-4 exclude boundary points. Fessler discussion printed554/PDF45 calls out the nonnegative Poisson boundary and refers to his1995 separate proof.

Augmentation information ordering in Section2 is asymptotic at an interior fit and may not order arbitrary augmentations. Claimed optimality is within the specified family, not over all algorithms. Reducing augmentation can make E/CM harder; less information, bigger early likelihood increments or more frequent E refreshes do not imply universally less elapsed time.

Printed537/PDF28 says optimizing each constrained model separately does not necessarily optimize the whole cycle spectral radius; order matters, and even improved asymptotic rate need not reduce CPU time, particularly near a boundary.

sage1994.abstract_interpretation: SAGE is a general likelihood or penalized-likelihood optimization framework using sequential parameter subsets and potentially different smaller hidden-data spaces. Its abstract reports monotone objective improvement, asymptotic rates and sufficient norm-convergence conditions, with Gaussian-signal and Poisson-imaging demonstrations. Author errata materially qualify the rate proof and update pseudocode.

mechanism.locator: Section II A-C, internal/PDF pp.2-3, Equations 1-7 and Definition 2
mechanism.note: For Phi(theta)=log p(y;theta)-P(theta), choose a parameter index subset S and an admissible hidden X^S satisfying p(y,x;theta)=p(y|x;theta_rest)p(x;theta). The observation channel must be independent of theta_S at fixed complement. It may depend on the complement, and combining all such hidden spaces need not yield one admissible complete-data space for the entire parameter vector. Compute current conditional expected log p(X^S;theta_S,theta_rest_current), subtract the penalty at that same fixed complement, and maximize over feasible theta_S. Copy unchanged complement; refresh expectations for the next selected subset. A generalized step can merely increase this surrogate. Optional extra E/M subiterations are permitted.

The Jensen/conditional-entropy argument makes each valid block surrogate improvement a lower bound on objective improvement. Index groups may be individual coordinates, rows/columns or overlapping/general blocks, with appropriate convergence coverage conditions. Choosing X^S=Y recovers grouped coordinate ascent; ordinary full-parameter EM is another special case. Parallelism, hidden-space information and ease of M step trade off; no universal CPU ordering follows.

Poisson observed mean is sum_k a_nk lambda_k+r_n with nonnegative coefficients, intensities and known background. ML-SAGE-1 updates one intensity using the latest predicted means and immediately updates those means. ML-SAGE-2 sets z_k=min_{n:a_nk>0} r_n/a_nk and hides independent Poisson components of rates a_nk(lambda_k+z_k) and r_n-a_nk z_k+sum_{j!=k}a_nj lambda_j. The update is max((lambda_k+z_k)*e_k/a_dotk-z_k,0), where e_k=sum_n a_nk*y_n/current_mean_n. Positive denominators and nonempty sensitivity support are required. The aggregate of all per-pixel spaces is not one joint complete-data space. The old-value overwrite in the displayed loop is explicitly retracted by author errata; current values of other pixels must be retained.

For Y=A theta+epsilon with Gaussian covariance Pi and quadratic penalty theta^T P theta/2, the objective Hessian is H=A^T Pi^-1 A+P. SAGE can associate all noise variance with the selected signal, while the described ordinary EM splits noise across p components. The resulting one-coordinate SAGE update equals Gauss-Seidel coordinate optimization for the quadratic objective and accommodates non-diagonal P. Positivity constraints require their own treatment. The iteration matrices permit scoped convergence analysis when H is positive definite.

Norm-convergence analysis assumes a cyclic collection covering every parameter, an interior fixed point and interior subproblem maximizers, twice differentiable surrogates, invertible conditional curvature and explicit nonexpansive/contraction bounds in a fixed transformed norm. The region is local in general. The paper explicitly says its interior theorem does not apply to Poisson maxima with zero components and refers to a later boundary-aware proof. Lower hidden information is a design motivation; the broad ordering argument invokes the same proof as the corrected Theorem 2 and should not be promoted without its qualifications.

sage1995.abstract_interpretation: The follow-up develops sequential hidden-space algorithms for penalized Poisson reconstruction, including an improved per-pixel design using other pixels as pseudobackground. It expands the general SAGE formulation to surrogate functions and supplies nonnegative-boundary convergence conditions. Neither the historical comparisons nor the convergence theorem applies without its stated objective and regularity assumptions.

mechanism.note: The generalized framework chooses a block and a surrogate phi such that its improvement lower-bounds the improvement in the actual penalized objective with all other parameters fixed. Maximizing the surrogate then gives ascent. Statistical hidden-space construction is a special case. Admissible hidden spaces can now depend on the current iteration/parameter anchor; their observation channel must remain independent of the active block during its update. Conditional expectation uses the full current parameter state. Bounded objective values converge but that alone does not imply parameter convergence.

Poisson mean is A lambda+r with known nonnegative background, nonnegative A and positive per-pixel sensitivity sums. Simultaneous EM assigns background across all pixels subject to sum_k a_nk*m_k<=r_n. Sequential SAGE can instead allocate up to r_n+sum_{j!=k}a_nj*lambda_j to the currently selected pixel, requiring a_nk*z_k<=that quantity. TypeIII TableI uses one selected pixel per iteration and immediately updates predicted counts; it does not restore previously updated coordinates to an old outer-loop vector.

The hidden split uses rates a_nk*(lambda_k+z_k) and r_n-a_nk*z_k+sum_{j!=k}a_nj*lambda_j. With e_k=sum_n a_nk*y_n/current_mean_n, the ML update is max((lambda_k+z_k)*e_k/a_dotk-z_k,0). SAGE1 takes z=0; SAGE2 uses min r_n/a_nk; SAGE3 uses the current other-pixel pseudobackground min_n[(r_n+sum_{j!=k}a_nj*lambda_j)/a_nk]. Only rows with nonzero a_nk enter the minimum. SAGE3 is therefore usable with zero physical background. Freeze this chosen z within the current conditional update and recompute as specified at the next step.

For symmetric neighbor weights and quadratic smoothness penalty, the one-pixel surrogate derivative is -a_dotk+e_k*(lambda_old_k+z_k)/(lambda_k+z_k)-beta*sum_j w_kj*(lambda_k-lambda_j_current). Its constrained maximizer is the positive root or zero. The displayed quadratic root requires nonzero beta times neighbor-weight sum; unpenalized or isolated-pixel limits require the ML formula instead. Stable quadratic evaluation matters; the authors say actual code uses a numerically stable formula and four alternating raster orders. No code was inspected.

The comparison GEM cycles coordinate updates of one fixed expected-complete objective, while SAGE immediately refreshes predicted counts for subsequent conditional expectations. One-step-late penalty evaluation and arbitrary gradient steps are not intrinsically monotone; a line search can enforce improvement. Do not equate them merely because all use coordinate or EM-related updates.

convergence_and_corrections.note: The global constrained result requires continuous differentiable strictly concave objective, bounded upper-level sets, the improvement inequality, strictly concave differentiable surrogates, matching first derivatives, conditional KKT updates, uniform positive surrogate curvature on bounded sets and bounded-gap recurring coordinate coverage. Author errata strengthen continuity of the mixed derivative to both arguments. These yield the unique constrained maximizer and permit boundary values; arbitrary nonconcave objectives are outside this conclusion.

It supplies both theoretical matrix identities and executable algorithm descriptions; covariance computation is distinct from changing the point estimator or accelerating fitting.
secm.identity: SupplementedEM (Meng/Rubin1991) and SupplementedECM (vanDyk/Meng/Rubin1995) have separate identities. Section3.1 explicitly supplies the SEM implementation as a special case of SECM with one joint Q maximization and CM Jacobian zero. The original1991 PDF remained inaccessible403 and is not claimed fully read; this complete1995 primary followup supports the narrowly stated SEM mechanism. SEM here is not stochastic EM or structural equation modeling; SCM is a supplemented CM helper, not a structural causal model.
mechanism: Section2.1 printed57/PDF3 assumes an interior MLE throughout and targets inverse observed negative log-likelihood Hessian. Invertibility and suitable asymptotic regularity matter; this is no finite-sample coverage guarantee.

Section2.3 printed58-59/PDF4-5: at theta*, expected complete information Ic is the conditional expected negative complete-data Hessian, not an arbitrary population Fisher information. Missing information Im is the conditional missing-data score curvature; Io=Ic-Im. Their Jacobian has input-coordinate rows and output-coordinate columns, confirmed by Eq3.3.3. D_EM=Im Ic^-1, Io=(I-D_EM)Ic, Vobs=Ic^-1(I-D_EM)^-1. State convention explicitly because standard column-vector map differentiation transposes these products.

Section2.4 Eq2.4.1 printed59/PDF5: I-D_ECM=(I-D_EM)(I-D_CM). CM means the sweep optimizing the FROZEN Q/sufficient statistics at the converged fit, whereas ECM refreshes E before its sweep. Ic and constraint gradients yield analytic D_CM=P1...PS; partitioned CM Eq2.4.4 printed60/PDF6 uses lower triangular Gamma and block diagonal Upsilon of Ic: D_CM=-Gamma(Upsilon+Gamma^T)^-1, consistent with row-Jacobian convention.

Section2.5 printed60/PDF6: Io=(I-D_ECM)(I-D_CM)^-1 Ic; Vobs=Vcom(I-D_CM)(I-D_ECM)^-1 =Vcom+Vcom(D_ECM-D_CM)(I-D_ECM)^-1. Factors do not generally commute; plugging ECM's Jacobian into the simpler SEM identity is wrong unless the relevant CM contribution vanishes. D_CM=0 recovers SEM.

Section3.1-3.3 printed61-64/PDF7-10: obtain tightly converged theta* and final conditional expected sufficient statistics; compute Ic/Vcom; for each input coordinate i, replace only theta*_i by a nearby iterate value theta_i(t), take one complete ECM update (E then entire CM sweep), form r_ij=(updated_j-theta*_j)/(theta_i(t)-theta*_i). Stabilized coordinate-wise ratios estimate input-row/output-column D_ECM. For D_CM repeat the same perturbation but run ONLY the CM sweep with the final sufficient statistics fixed; alternatively evaluate analytic constraint formula. Then combine with Vcom using Eq2.5.3. Converging sequence may be saved or recomputed; rate probes are not just ratios of all-coordinate iterates.

For SEM use ordinary EM point fit, one unconstrained Q maximization, D_CM=0; estimate its EM map Jacobian with the same coordinate perturbations and use Vobs=Vcom(I-D_EM)^-1. It requires complete-data curvature in addition to the EM update routine, not merely a scalar EM convergence rate.

Section3.4/5.1 printed64,71-72/PDF10,17-18: map derivative precision requires more accurate theta* than point fitting alone; small denominators and finite subtraction matter. Source square-root tolerance guidance is heuristic and scale-dependent, not a certified universal error bound. Inspect unsymmetrized covariance/increment before hiding errors through forced symmetrization.

Section5.2 printed72/PDF18: a multicycle-ECM sequence can locate theta* and supply perturbation points, but supplement calculation still differentiates the ordinary single-E ECM map and corresponding frozen-Q CM map. Do not substitute the multicycle Jacobian into Eq2.5.3.

Section5.3 printed72-73/PDF18-19: components solved exactly with no missing information can make the original ratio denominator zero. A special treatment computes the affected conditional variance increment and embeds it in the full matrix; do not divide blindly. Finite exact-to-zero paths can pose a similar numerical issue.
limitations: Symmetry is a useful necessary diagnostic, not sufficient proof of correctness, statistical calibration, or attainment of the correct likelihood optimum. Section5.1 rhetorically treats symmetric output as virtually assuring correctness; retain the diagnostic while refusing that universal conclusion. A common scaling error in complete and observed information can preserve symmetry and still give incorrect variances; a finite check is planned.

At boundary or nonidentifiable/singular fits, inverse curvature and the linear-rate identity can be undefined or statistically inappropriate. Slow convergence and eigenvalues near one amplify differentiation errors. No guarantee of finite-sample interval coverage or full posterior inference.

Primary mathematical identity is broader than exponential families, but the straightforward sufficient-statistics implementation in Section3.2 explicitly assumes an exponential-family complete model. Other models may require expected Hessian integration and additional numerical work.

Published incorrect conditional moments that ignore observed Y1 are corrected on pp65-66. The source's example is not a new clinical or predictive performance result.

native_neighbors.definition: An entropy-tempered generalization of expectation maximization for finite latent-state models that alternates powered latent-joint responsibilities with weighted complete-log-likelihood parameter updates at a positive inverse temperature.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes the deterministic free-energy fitting procedure described by Hofmann, with his held-out inverse-annealing schedule as an explicit realization. Ordinary EM is its beta=1 case. The procedure changes responsibilities and parameter fitting; it is neither replica-exchange MCMC nor a supervised confidence-mask schedule, and it does not introduce a new topic-model probability family. The short TEM acronym is not asserted as a globally unambiguous alias. Compared all 442 pinned AIO labels and scoped synonyms and 418 preceding native IDs, names and aliases. An additional broad LDA search returned 289 worktree and 237 main lines before the preceding batch merged; all 84 distinct contents were read, covering the existing classifier, topic-context references, unrelated programming mnemonics and namespace abbreviations. The 35 contextual YAMLs were read or byte-verified after documented full reading. Absence is bounded to this snapshot, maintained corpus and inspected semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Responsibilities require a positive finite normalizer for each observed x. At positive beta, zero latent-joint entries remain zero; the beta-to-zero limit is uniform only over the positive support. beta=0 makes the displayed parameter objective independent of eta and is not included as an ordinary M-step.
This record concerns finite latent-state sums. Raising a continuous latent density to a power below one need not preserve integrability; that extension requires its own conditions.

Exact block updates concern fixed-beta free energy. They do not guarantee monotonic ordinary likelihood for beta different from one, global optimality, posterior calibration or held-out improvement. Changing beta does not optimize one unchanged objective.

The inverse-annealing schedule decreases beta after an ordinary-EM start and uses held-out decisions. It is not the same schedule as conventional deterministic-annealing cooling, and it is not a stochastic sampling transition with an invariant target. Schedule thresholds and multiplicative factors require an implementation choice.

The source’s perplexity and retrieval comparisons concern selected historical corpora and settings. No automatic prevention of overfitting, speedup, universal benefit or author-code reproduction is claimed.

claims.statement: For observations x with multiplicities n_x, finite latent states z, model parameters eta and a positive inverse temperature beta, minimize F_beta(q,eta)=sum_x n_x*sum_z q_xz*[log q_xz-beta*log p_eta(x,z)]. For fixed eta, on positive joint support use q_xz=p_eta(x,z)^beta/sum_j p_eta(x,j)^beta. For fixed q and beta>0, minimizing F_beta over eta is equivalent to maximizing the expected complete log likelihood; in PLSA this gives the usual normalized expected-count M-step with the tempered responsibilities. At beta=1 the E-step is the ordinary posterior. With 0<beta<1 it is flatter on its positive support. Hofmann’s inverse-annealing schedule first runs early-stopped EM at beta=1, then reduces beta multiplicatively, continues iterations while held-out performance improves, and stops decreasing beta when further improvements cease. At fixed beta, exact block updates optimize that temperature’s free energy; changing beta changes the objective.

claims.statement: For sample covariance S=N^(-1)sum_n(t_n-mu)(t_n-mu)^T at the sample-mean mu, take its q leading eigenpairs U_q,Lambda_q. The likelihood solution has sigma^2 equal to the mean of the d-q discarded eigenvalues and W=U_q(Lambda_q-sigma^2 I)^(1/2)R for any orthogonal R. Rank(S)>q ensures positive residual variance. Tied eigenvalues can make loading columns vanish: for spectrum (2,1,1) and q=2, sigma^2=1 and the effective loading rank is one. Neither the columns nor latent coordinates are uniquely identified.

claims.statement: With M=W^T W+sigma^2 I, the latent posterior is Normal(M^(-1)W^T(t-mu),sigma^2 M^(-1)). Mapping its mean back through W generally shrinks the observation within the loading subspace; it is not the ordinary orthogonal PCA reconstruction. When W has full column rank, W(W^T W)^(-1)M times the posterior mean, plus mu, recovers the orthogonal projection. The zero-noise limit loses a nonsingular ambient density for q<d.

evidence.locator: Equations 6 and 9 and Section 3.4, printed pp. 614-615 / PDF pp. 4-5; curator finite shrinkage and rank qualification

claims.statement: The E-step computes posterior first and second latent moments using the old W and noise variance. Exact well-defined EM makes likelihood nondecreasing, but a zero-loading initialization can remain stationary at an inferior isotropic solution. The existence of a principal-eigenspace maximum does not guarantee successful convergence from every initialization.

Alternatively, the paper gives a two-stage generalized EM update using one inner latent-variable EM step, with the new mean, old loading/noise parameters and fixed outer responsibilities. claims.statement: Specify an expanded complete-data density p_X(y_com|theta_star,alpha) that recovers the original augmentation at alpha_0 and whose observed density equals the original density at theta=R(theta_star,alpha). At each iteration embed the current theta with alpha_0, compute expanded conditional sufficient moments, maximize expanded Q over the expanded parameters, reduce by R, and reset the auxiliary parameter to alpha_0 for the next E step. The observed-density equality makes expanded EM ascent transfer to the original likelihood.

claims.statement: For a p-dimensional t distribution with fixed positive degrees of freedom nu, old latent weights are w_i=(nu+p)/(nu+delta_i), with delta_i the old scatter-based squared Mahalanobis distance. Ordinary EM uses the weighted mean and scatter sum_i w_i(y_i-mu_new)(y_i-mu_new)^T/N. Expanding the mean of the latent gamma scale yields alpha_new=sum_i w_i/N. Dividing the expanded scatter by alpha_new reduces to the original t model, giving denominator sum_i w_i instead of N; the next iteration resets alpha to one. This normalization follows from the stated expansion and reduction.

evidence.locator: Section 2, pp.756-758 / PDF pp.3-5

claims.statement: For y|z~Normal(z,1), z~Normal(theta,sigma_squared), with known positive sigma_squared, ordinary EM updates theta to m=(theta_old+sigma_squared*y)/(1+sigma_squared). Expanding the conditional observation mean to z+alpha gives theta_star_new=m and alpha_new=y-m. The reduction theta_star+alpha returns theta_new=y in one iteration, while ordinary EM contracts its error by 1/(1+sigma_squared). This exact example does not establish one-step convergence for other expansions.

native_neighbors.name: Sparse additive generative model
native_neighbors.definition: A generative model family for categorical text data that forms word probabilities by normalizing a background log-frequency vector plus sparse component deviations, allowing multiple generative facets to combine additively in log space.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: SAGE here denotes Eisenstein, Ahmed and Xing’s sparse additive generative construction, not Sage mathematical software or graph-neural aggregation. Its classification, topic and multifaceted uses share this parameterization; it is not synonymous with all naive Bayes models, sparse dictionary learning, sparse topic proportions or an arithmetic mixture of component word distributions. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 352 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; worktree returned 15 lines and main 19. All 16 unique matched contents were read: DocNADE contrasts, frontier and review references, plus four ignored-environment Sage/Pygments entries unrelated to AI SAGE. Twenty-one exact AIO nodes and four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Sparsity concerns log deviations. Finite logits still give positive word probabilities, and even zero-deviation words can change absolute probability through normalization; their relative odds remain those of the background when their deviations agree.

Additive log facets yield multiplicative unnormalized effects, not an arithmetic probability mixture. The model family does not require every document to have a single observed class or prohibit latent variables.

The Jeffreys-prior paragraph on PDF p.4 prints expected inverse variance equal to eta squared. Its preceding Gamma moment and b=eta squared/(a-1) instead give 1/eta squared for nonzero eta, with a>1 and positive scale. The printed final identity is not adopted; zero deviations require a limiting/numerical treatment. The improper prior is not represented as a normalized marginal distribution.

The paper warns that warm-starting tightly coupled deviation/variance updates can lock in early sparsity patterns. Neither approximate inference nor Newton updates establish global convergence or calibrated posterior uncertainty.

The single-component rank-one Hessian argument is not asserted unchanged for sums over multiple facet combinations. No author implementation, universal predictive advantage or numerical benchmark result is certified.

claims.statement: For a component k, set p(w=i|k) proportional to exp(m_i+eta_ki), normalizing over the vocabulary. Multiple selected facets contribute a sum of their deviation vectors before this normalization; no additional token-level switch is needed to choose which facet generates the word. This does not remove latent topic assignments used by a topic-model variant. The paper places sparsity-inducing priors on deviations, using zero-mean Gaussian components with latent variances: an exponential variance prior gives a Laplace marginal, while an alternative improper Jeffreys prior gives a different shrinkage construction. It combines MAP estimates of deviations with variational treatment of other latent quantities. For a single component and fixed expected precisions, the gradient is observed or expected counts minus total count times word probabilities minus the precision-weighted deviations; its Hessian is a rank-one term minus a diagonal term, enabling the reported efficient Newton update.
